evaluation_protocol.fold_generator: gems61.holdout.make_folds; hide 20% of whole 8-connected catalogue components, 3 px context buffer, four spatial quadrants, seed 20261011
evaluation_protocol.catalogue_features: None are used by the candidate. In every fold the visible catalogue is masked pixel-exactly in the scored domain; any future catalogue-derived feature may use visible faults only.
evaluation_protocol.metric: pooled DTI, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m triangular kernel
evaluation_protocol.interval: paired percentile bootstrap of globally aligned 20 km spatial blocks, 1,000 draws, seed 520810; conditional on fixed folds and catalogue truth, not a leaderboard interval
controls: random straight lines at the same emitted-pixel budget and footprint
unfiltered HGM step maxima at the same budget
synthetic buried intrabasement-density body with no fault displacement
evaluation_protocol.lane_recovery: Count withheld 8-connected fault components for which at least 50% of component pixels fall in the deepest 40% of the candidate's own inversion. A segment is recovered when at least one of its pixels inside that deep mask lies within 300 m of a candidate pixel. Compare against matched random lines. No band 15 is used.
evaluation_protocol.leakage_canary: Run each registered feature alone against withheld catalogue pixels; any AUC > 0.90 is leakage-suspect and blocks promotion until resolved.
evaluation_protocol.uniqueness: Fresh full-registry Spearman surface comparison before placement and 3 px dot-overlap comparison on the final output. Follow the standing stop limits: rho > 0.90 or >70% of candidate dots within 3 px of any registry raster is a duplicate and stops promotion.
evaluation_protocol.run_limit: At most three experiments or two hours, whichever comes first. Slot recommendation is a separate selector decision.

frozen_primary.name: Signed one-sided flank-offset persistence of inverted basement steps

inversion_prior.stabilizer: W(k)=1/(1+(k/kc)^2), Oldenburg/Wiener low-pass; filter_order=2, kc_scale=1.0, kc=1/(2*z0); first Parker-Oldenburg slab iterate only
inversion_prior.calibration_status: uncalibrated; fixed before holdout, not fitted against band 15, GP-1012, or labels

frozen_primary.physical_signature: At a horizontal-gradient maximum of the inverted depth surface, sample the signed depth difference on opposite sides of the local gradient normal at 2 km and 4 km. Require the same downthrow sign at both apertures and a predeclared persistence ratio min(|delta_2km|, |delta_4km|)/(max(|delta_2km|, |delta_4km|)+epsilon) >= 0.60. Emit a 3-pixel ribbon around surviving step crests; thin to 40,000 positive pixels with 3-pixel minimum separation.
frozen_primary.catalogue_missing_fault_rationale: A concealed normal-fault block boundary can lack a mapped surface scarp while retaining a persistent one-sided offset in the basement interface. This tests displacement continuity, not simple gradient strength.
frozen_primary.named_non_fault_mimic: A finite-width intrabasement mafic/granitic density body or intrusive contact can create a gravity edge without any fault. Its paired opposite-polarity edges should lose same-sign flank contrast as the sampling aperture spans the body; the control will include a synthetic buried density sheet with no basement displacement.
frozen_primary.difference_from_existing: Local H61 methods already locate HGM maxima, measure throw and dilate ribbons. Sibling GEMSDOE52 R2 uses gradient-normal anti-alignment between band 13 gravity and band 15 cover at 1/3/8 px, plus cross-view interactions. H61U-H1 uses band 13 only, inverts it to basement depth, then samples signed depth displacement on the HGM normal at 2 km and 4 km; it uses no band 15 and no learned cross-layer feature.

ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: Signed basement-depth contrast at 2 km and 4 km across each HGM crest; same polarity and >=0.60 magnitude persistence; emit a 3-pixel ribbon.
ranked_hypotheses.why_catalogue_misses_it: A buried basin-interior fault can offset basement without preserving an exposed scarp; persistent one-sided displacement is the target.
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Finite-width intrabasement mafic/granitic body or intrusive contact; paired edges can imitate a local step.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_existing: Not another HGM/throw threshold and not sibling R2's band-13/band-15 normal anti-alignment. Use sign-consistent 2 km/4 km cross-step flank persistence from the band-13-only inverted depth surface.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Along-strike basement-throw taper at concealed fault tips
layers: band 13: iso_grav_anom only; derived inverted basement depth
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: For each connected depth-HGM step segment at least 20 km long, sample signed 2 km normal throw every 400 m along strike. Require one polarity over the central 60% and a monotone or single-hump displacement envelope whose median absolute throw in each terminal 20% is <=0.20 of the segment maximum; do not use catalogue traces to define or orient segments.
ranked_hypotheses.why_catalogue_misses_it: A fault buried beneath basin fill can have a real basement displacement tapering to subsurface tips even when no surface rupture or scarp is mapped; the scale-space tip geometry is present in the inverted interface.
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: A finite intrusive body or density sheet can produce edge responses that taper near its ends; this is an explicit ambiguity, not a claim that taper proves faulting.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_existing: Local H61 code thresholds pointwise throw and tests persistence across Gaussian scales 0/2/5; GEMSDOE52 R2 tests cross-layer normal orientation at 1/3/8 px, and H53/H54 test trace continuation. H61U-H2 instead tests the along-strike envelope of signed basement displacement at subsurface step tips, without band 15 or catalogue geometry.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_rank: 2 of 3; low-to-medium potential, uncertain and unquantified
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: medium (component graph plus fixed along-strike displacement-profile test)
ranked_hypotheses.data_obtainability: Only cached band 13 and the pinned competition grid are required locally; GP-1012 remains the separate, unavailable depth-scale calibration reference.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Local gravity source-class comparison: basement step versus buried density sheet
layers: band 13: iso_grav_anom only; derived inverted basement depth for candidate normals
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: At each candidate depth-HGM normal, fit the preregistered one-dimensional band-13 gravity profile with two label-free forward models: a Parker basement-interface step and a finite buried density-sheet/contact model. Retain a fault-step candidate only when the step model wins by a fixed information-criterion margin (BIC difference >=10), with all nuisance ranges frozen before any holdout evaluation.
ranked_hypotheses.why_catalogue_misses_it: A real basement offset under alluvial cover is not necessarily mapped at the surface; the gravity profile can still contain its source-shape signature.
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: A finite-width mafic/granitic intrusive body or lithologic contact inside basement; the competing density-sheet forward model is intended to reject this non-fault cause.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_existing: Existing H61 methods detect, threshold, corridor, or corroborate depth-HGM edges; none compares raw gravity profiles against competing basement-interface-relief and intrabasement-density forward models. It uses no band 15 and no catalogue-derived feature.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_rank: 3 of 3; uncertain/low potential because gravity source non-uniqueness may dominate
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: high (two physical forward models, nuisance bounds, model-selection validation)
ranked_hypotheses.data_obtainability: Only cached band 13 and the pinned competition grid are required locally; GP-1012 is still needed for any depth-scale calibration and is not currently available in full.

selection_rule: Test only frozen H61U-H1 with the shared evaluator. Report the fixed HGM-only, random-line and synthetic-density-body controls in the same paired run. H61U-H2 and H61U-H3 are untested alternatives, not fallback arms; do not substitute them based on H1 results. Any follow-up requires a new preregistration and remaining experiment budget. The random-line control uses the fixed seed in evaluation_protocol; the density-sheet mimic uses the geometry and physical values frozen under frozen_primary.synthetic_density_mimic_control.
